name: accept
synopsis: int accept(int sockfd, struct sockaddr *_Nullable restrict addr, socklen_t *_Nullable restrict addrlen);
int accept4(int sockfd, struct sockaddr *_Nullable restrict addr, socklen_t *_Nullable restrict addrlen, int flags);
description: The accept() system call extracts the first connection request on the queue of pending connections for a listening socket, creates a new connected socket, and returns a new file descriptor. The original socket remains unaffected. It is used with connection-based socket types like SOCK_STREAM.

parameters.name: sockfd
parameters.description: The file descriptor of the listening socket, created with socket(2), bound with bind(2), and listening with listen(2)

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Pointer to a sockaddr structure to receive the address of the peer socket; if NULL, no address is returned

parameters.name: addrlen
parameters.description: Pointer to the size of the addr structure; it is a value-result argument that is updated with the actual size on return

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Flags for accept4() only, such as SOCK_NONBLOCK or SOCK_CLOEXEC to set nonblocking or close-on-exec behavior

return_value.success: Returns a file descriptor for the accepted socket (a nonnegative integer)
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, errno is set, and addrlen is left unchanged

errors.description: The socket is marked nonblocking and no connections are present to be accepted
sockfd is not an open file descriptor
The addr argument is not in a writable part of the user address space
The system call was interrupted by a signal before a valid connection arrived
Socket is not listening for connections, or addrlen is invalid (e.g., negative), or invalid flags for accept4()
The per-process limit on the number of open file descriptors has been reached
The system-wide limit on the total number of open files has been reached
Insufficient resources were available in the system to perform the operation
The file descriptor sockfd does not refer to a socket
The referenced socket is not of type SOCK_STREAM

bugs: On Linux, the new socket does not inherit file status flags like O_NONBLOCK from the listening socket, differing from BSD behavior. Additionally, there may not always be a connection waiting after a readability event, potentially causing accept() to block unexpectedly.
versions: accept() first appeared in 4.2BSD; accept4() in Linux 2.6.28, glibc 2.10
posix_compliance: POSIX.1-2008 for accept(); Linux for accept4()
